entries.title: Treating melatonin as a proven aid for PCOS or premenstrual symptoms
entries.take: Pooled trials in polycystic ovary syndrome found no effect on hormones or metabolic markers, and no trial has tested it for premenstrual symptoms.
entries.body: McDonald's 2020 article was optimistic about polycystic ovary syndrome on the strength of small trials. One, in 56 women taking 5 mg twice a day for 12 weeks, reported lower testosterone and less excess hair growth. A 2024 meta-analysis of six randomised trials found only a rise in antioxidant capacity, with no pooled effect on testosterone, hair growth score, insulin, lipids or pregnancy rate. His article predates it. For premenstrual symptoms he states plainly that nobody had tested melatonin and that his suggestion was speculation. Both conditions are diagnosed and treated by doctors.
do: Discuss PCOS or severe premenstrual symptoms with a doctor before trying any supplement.

entries.title: In menopausal women melatonin helped sleep mainly where sleep was already poor
entries.take: A systematic review of 24 studies found better sleep quality in postmenopausal women with existing sleep problems, and symptom relief at 3 mg or more.
entries.body: The review covered 1,173 participants. It found a fair amount of evidence for favourable effects on bone density and body mass index, improved sleep recordings and subjective sleep quality in postmenopausal women whose sleep was already impaired, and improvement in one or more areas of menopausal symptoms at doses of 3 mg and above. It found no independent effect on blood pressure or glucose markers, and some evidence that triglycerides rise. Menopausal symptoms and sleep problems have several causes and several treatments. A doctor or pharmacist should be asked first, including about interactions.
do: Raise menopausal sleep problems with a doctor; ask about melatonin there if you wish.

entries.title: Iron deficiency is common in female athletes and is found by a blood test
entries.take: A systematic review reports that up to 60 percent of female athletes experience iron deficiency, which lowered endurance performance by 3 to 4 percent.
entries.body: The review covered 23 studies and 669 high-level female athletes, and defined deficiency as serum ferritin under 40 micrograms per litre. Endurance performance and aerobic capacity improved when deficient athletes were treated with iron. Effects on strength and anaerobic power were inconsistent, and most studies had 20 or fewer athletes per group. Fatigue has many causes, and iron status cannot be judged from symptoms. Iron is a treatment for a measured deficiency, so the dose and form are for a doctor to set after a blood test.
do: Ask a doctor for a blood test if you have persistent, unexplained fatigue.
Do not start iron tablets on a guess.

handelsman-2018.title: Circulating Testosterone as the Hormonal Basis of Sex Differences in Athletic Performance
handelsman-2018.support: From puberty onward a clear sex difference in athletic performance emerges as circulating testosterone concentrations rise in men because testes produce 30 times more testosterone than before puberty with circulating testosterone exceeding 15-fold that of women at any age. These dichotomies largely account for the sex differences in muscle mass and strength and circulating hemoglobin levels that result in at least an 8% to 12% ergogenic advantage in men. Women with polycystic ovary syndrome are overrepresented in elite athletics.

hunter-2023.title: The Biological Basis of Sex Differences in Athletic Performance: Consensus Statement for the American College of Sports Medicine
hunter-2023.support: For athletic events and sports relying on endurance, muscle strength, speed, and power, males typically outperform females by 10%-30% depending on the requirements of the event. These sex differences in performance emerge with the onset of puberty and coincide with the increase in endogenous sex steroid hormones, in particular testosterone in males, which increases 30-fold by adulthood, but remains low in females.

mcdonald-female-vs-male-physiology.title: Female vs Male Physiology
mcdonald-female-vs-male-physiology.support: Backs the points that hormone levels differ widely between the sexes, that the monthly cycle is what sets female physiology apart, and his list of things that alter a woman's hormonal picture.

miller-1993.title: Gender differences in strength and muscle fiber characteristics
miller-1993.journal: European Journal of Applied Physiology and Occupational Physiology
miller-1993.support: Eight men and eight women. The women were approximately 52% and 66% as strong as the men in the upper and lower body respectively. The women had 45, 41, 30 and 25% smaller muscle CSAs for the biceps brachii, total elbow flexors, vastus lateralis and total knee extensors respectively. No significant gender difference was found in the strength to CSA ratio for elbow flexion or knee extension.

nuzzo-2023.title: Narrative Review of Sex Differences in Muscle Strength, Endurance, Activation, Size, Fiber Type, and Strength Training Participation Rates, Preferences, Motivations, Injuries, and Neuromuscular Adaptations
nuzzo-2023.support: In adults, sex differences in strength are more pronounced in upper-body than lower-body muscles and in concentric than eccentric contractions. Greater male than female strength is not because of higher voluntary activation but to greater muscle mass and type II fiber areas. Men and women increase muscle size and strength after weeks of strength training, but women experience greater relative strength improvements depending on age and muscle group.

nuzzo-2024-fibre.title: Sex differences in skeletal muscle fiber types: A meta-analysis
nuzzo-2024-fibre.support: Data from 2875 men and 2452 women, who participated in 110 studies, were analyzed. Men exhibited greater cross-sectional areas for all fiber types (g = 0.40-1.68). Women exhibited greater Type I and MHC I distribution percentages (g = -0.13, -0.44); greater Type I and MHC I area percentages (g = -0.53, -0.69).

refalo-2025.title: Sex differences in absolute and relative changes in muscle size following resistance training in healthy adults: a systematic review with Bayesian meta-analysis
refalo-2025.support: 29 studies were included in the statistical analysis. Absolute increases in muscle size slightly favoured males compared to females (SMD = 0.19 (95% HDI: 0.11 to 0.28)), however, relative increases in muscle size were similar between sexes (Exp. % Change of lnRR = 0.69% (95% HDI: -1.50% to 2.88%)). Outcomes were not influenced by RT experience of participants. Absolute hypertrophy of upper-body but not lower-body regions was favoured in males.

hamadeh-2005.title: Estrogen Supplementation Reduces Whole Body Leucine and Carbohydrate Oxidation and Increases Lipid Oxidation in Men during Endurance Exercise
hamadeh-2005.journal: The Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism
hamadeh-2005.support: Healthy active men exhibit higher rates of carbohydrate (CHO) and leucine oxidation and lower rates of lipid oxidation compared with their female counterparts both at rest and during moderate intensity endurance exercise. In 12 recreationally active men, estrogen supplementation significantly decreased CHO oxidation by 5-16% and leucine oxidation by 16%, whereas it significantly increased lipid oxidation by 22-44% at rest and during exercise.

elliott-sale-2021.title: Methodological Considerations for Studies in Sport and Exercise Science with Women as Participants: A Working Guide for Standards of Practice for Research on Women
elliott-sale-2021.support: The vast majority of high-quality sport and exercise science data have been derived from studies with men as participants. Full text: define eumenorrhea as menstrual cycle lengths of 21 to 35 days resulting in 9 or more consecutive periods per year; oligomenorrhea as cycle length over 35 days; secondary amenorrhea as the absence of 3 or more consecutive periods in non-pregnant women with past menses; use the term withdrawal bleed rather than period for the bleed experienced by OCP users.

roberts-2020-sex.title: Sex Differences in Resistance Training: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
roberts-2020-sex.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
roberts-2020-sex.support: The analysis of hypertrophy comprised 12 outcomes from 10 studies with no significant difference between males and females (ES = 0.07; P = 0.31). The analysis of upper-body strength comprised 19 outcomes from 17 studies with a significant effect favoring females (ES = -0.60; P = 0.002). The analysis of lower-body strength comprised 23 outcomes from 23 studies with no significant difference between sexes (ES = -0.21; P = 0.20).

mcdonald-strength-muscle-mass-women.title: Strength and Muscle Mass Increases in Young Women
mcdonald-strength-muscle-mass-women.support: Backs his view that beginners of both sexes gain similar percentages, that visible size change in women is small and follows strength, and that fear of size fades once strength rises.

jones-2021.title: Sex Differences in Adaptations in Muscle Strength and Size Following Resistance Training in Older Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
jones-2021.support: 30 studies were included (1410 participants; 651 males, 759 females). Females gained more relative lower-body strength than males (g = -0.21) but there were no differences in relative change for upper-body strength or relative muscle size. Males gained more absolute upper-body strength (g = 0.48), absolute lower-body strength (g = 0.33), and absolute muscle size (g = 0.45). The interpretation of sex-dependent adaptations is heavily influenced by the presentation of the results in either an absolute or relative context.

hagstrom-2020.title: The Effect of Resistance Training in Women on Dynamic Strength and Muscular Hypertrophy: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis
hagstrom-2020.support: A total of 24 studies met the inclusion criteria. Large-effect sizes were found for upper body strength (Hedges' g = 1.70) and lower body strength (Hedges' g = 1.40). Following use of the Trim and Fill method, a large effect still remained for upper body strength (g = 1.07), although a medium effect was found for lower body strength (g = 0.52). A medium effect was found for muscular hypertrophy (g = 0.52, p = 0.002).

cureton-1988.title: Muscle hypertrophy in men and women
cureton-1988.support: Seven male experimental, 8 female experimental, and 7 control subjects were studied before and after a 16-wk weight training program. Strength increased significantly in ME and FE, respectively, on elbow flexion (36.2 and 59.2%), elbow extension (32.6 and 41.7%), knee flexion (12.8 and 24.4%), and knee extension (28.8 and 33.9%) tests. Percentage changes were not significantly different. Muscle CSA determined from computed tomography scanning of the upper arm rose 15.9 and 22.8%; no muscle hypertrophy occurred in the thigh of either group (2.9 and 2.9%).

harty-2019.title: Upper and lower thresholds of fat-free mass index in a large cohort of female collegiate athletes
harty-2019.support: 372 female collegiate athletes underwent body composition assessment via dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry. Average FFMI was 18.82±2.08 kg/m2. FFMI in rugby athletes was 20.09, cross country 16.56, Olympic weightlifting 19.69. The upper threshold for FFMI in female athletes (97.5th percentile) was 23.90 kg/m2.

blue-2019.title: Normative fat-free mass index values for a diverse sample of collegiate female athletes
blue-2019.support: A sample of 266 female athletes were included in analyses. For all females, mean FFMI was 16.9 ± 1.7 kg/m2, FFMI values ranged from 13.3 to 25.5 kg/m2. The XC athletes had the lowest FFMI (15.3 ± 0.96 kg/m2).

abe-1998.title: Gender differences in FFM accumulation and architectural characteristics of muscle
abe-1998.support: Skeletal muscle architectural characteristics and FFM were studied in 29 strength-trained female and 22 age- and height-matched male college athletes. Six female athletes had more than 60 kg of FFM, with the largest being 82.1 kg. We conclude that the theoretical upper limit of FFM accumulation and FFM-to-height ratio in women is greater than 80 kg and 0.44 kg.cm-1, respectively.

mcdonald-womens-muscular-potential.title: Women's Muscular Potential
mcdonald-womens-muscular-potential.support: Source of his working lean-mass-per-height figure for women, his reading of the 1998 outlier, the three-to-four-year estimate and the small monthly targets near the limit.

johnson-1990.title: A physiological comparison of female body builders and power lifters
johnson-1990.journal: The Journal of Sports Medicine and Physical Fitness
johnson-1990.support: Ten female body builders and ten female power lifters, all training a minimum of two years. FPL had significantly greater body weight (68.60 vs 56.47 kg) and relative fat (21.47 vs 13.51%). No significant differences were found for fat-free weight, strength or anaerobic power and capacity.

vanderploeg-2001.title: Body composition changes in female bodybuilders during preparation for competition
vanderploeg-2001.support: Five competitive bodybuilders (167.3 cm; 66.38 kg; 18.3 %BF) and five athletic females (166.9 cm; 55.94 kg; 19.1 %BF). A combination of underwater weighing, deuterium dilution and DXA bone mineral enabled %BF to be determined by a four compartment model. A 5.80 kg body mass loss by the bodybuilders as they prepared for competition was primarily due to a reduction in fat mass (-4.42 kg) as opposed to fat-free mass (-1.38 kg).

hagmar-2009.title: Hyperandrogenism May Explain Reproductive Dysfunction in Olympic Athletes
hagmar-2009.support: Ninety Swedish female Olympic athletes. Of all the athletes, 47% were using hormonal contraception. Menstrual dysfunction was common (27%) among those not using HC and, particularly, in endurance athletes. The most common diagnosis associated with MD was polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and not hypothalamic inhibition because of energy deficiency.

rickenlund-2003.title: Hyperandrogenicity is an alternative mechanism underlying oligomenorrhea or amenorrhea in female athletes and may improve physical performance
rickenlund-2003.support: A subgroup of 8 of 25 athletes with menstrual disturbances had significantly higher serum levels of free and total testosterone. The hyperandrogenic subgroup showed a more anabolic body composition, with higher total bone mineral density. We suggest that essential hyperandrogenism is an alternative mechanism underlying oligomenorrhea or amenorrhea in some female athletes.

burke-2018.title: Pitfalls of Conducting and Interpreting Estimates of Energy Availability in Free-Living Athletes
burke-2018.journal: International Journal of Sport Nutrition and Exercise Metabolism
burke-2018.support: Energy availability (EA) is defined as the energy available to support these basic physiological functions and good health once the energy cost of exercise is deducted from energy intake (EI), relative to an athlete's fat-free mass (FFM). Problems include the lack of a universal protocol for the calculation of EA, the resources needed to achieve estimates of each of the components of the equation, and the residual errors in these estimates. The lack of a clear definition of the value for EA that is considered low reflects problems around its measurement.

loucks-2003.title: Luteinizing Hormone Pulsatility Is Disrupted at a Threshold of Energy Availability in Regularly Menstruating Women
loucks-2003.journal: The Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism
loucks-2003.support: 29 young women; luteinizing hormone pulsatility was unaffected at 30 kcal/kg LBM/day of energy availability, and disrupted below this threshold.

desouza-2026.title: 2025 Update to the Female Athlete Triad Coalition Consensus Statement Part 1: State of the Science and Introduction of a New Adolescent Model
desouza-2026.support: The Triad is defined as three inter-related components including energy status, reproductive function, and bone health. Full text: an EA of approximately 45 kcal/kg FFM/day has been associated with the healthy end of the Triad continuum; in this revised Consensus Statement, the utility of an EA threshold is less supported than in previous position stands; many women with ovulatory cycles had EA levels below 30 kcal/kg FFM/day, and women with menstrual disturbances had EA levels above 30.

mountjoy-2023.title: 2023 International Olympic Committee’s (IOC) consensus statement on Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs)
mountjoy-2023.support: 2023 IOC consensus statement on Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport; health and performance outcomes of low energy availability in female and male athletes.

mcdonald-body-fat-ea-hormones.title: Body Fat Energy Availability or Hormones
mcdonald-body-fat-ea-hormones.support: Backs the account that a critical body fat level was first blamed for lost cycles and that energy availability turned out to be the cause; his threshold figures predate newer trials.

lieberman-2018.title: Menstrual Disruption with Exercise Is Not Linked to an Energy Availability Threshold
lieberman-2018.support: Thirty-five sedentary, ovulatory women age 18 to 24 yr completed a diet and exercise intervention over three menstrual cycles. The likelihood of a MD decreased by 9% for each unit increase in EA (odds ratio, 0.91; 95% confidence interval, 0.84-0.98). No specific value of EA emerged as a threshold below which MD were induced.

williams-2026.title: 2025 Update to the Female Athlete Triad Coalition Consensus Statement Part 2: Clinical Guidelines for Screening, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Return to Play for Adolescents and Adults
williams-2026.support: Recent research supports the adoption of revised criteria for defining and treating energy deficiency, moving away from the concept of an energy-availability threshold. Energy deficiency-induced menstrual disturbances can be reversed with a moderate increase in food intake and modest weight gain, but restoration of menses alone is not associated with high rates of ovulation or increased ovarian steroid levels until multiple consecutive normal length menstrual cycles are achieved. Full text: an increase in energy intake between 300 and 600 kcal/day will likely initiate reproductive recovery; combined oral contraceptive pills may mask spontaneous menstrual resumption.

gordon-2017.title: Functional Hypothalamic Amenorrhea: An Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline
gordon-2017.journal: The Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism
gordon-2017.support: FHA is a form of chronic anovulation, not due to identifiable organic causes, but often associated with stress, weight loss, excessive exercise, or a combination thereof. Investigations should include assessment of systemic and endocrinologic etiologies, as FHA is a diagnosis of exclusion. A multidisciplinary treatment approach is necessary, including medical, dietary, and mental health support.

desouza-2021.title: Randomised controlled trial of the effects of increased energy intake on menstrual recovery in exercising women with menstrual disturbances: the ‘REFUEL’ study
desouza-2021.support: A modest increase in daily energy intake (330 ± 65 kcal/day; 18 ± 4%) is sufficient to induce menstrual recovery in exercising women with Oligo/Amen. 12 months of increased energy intake in 76 exercising women with menstrual disturbances. The Oligo/Amen + Cal group was more likely to experience menses during the intervention than the control group (hazard ratio = 1.91 [1.27, 2.89]).

mcdonald-menstrual-cycle-energy-balance.title: The Menstrual Cycle and Determinants of Energy Intake
mcdonald-menstrual-cycle-energy-balance.support: His walk through a 2007 review of appetite and expenditure across the cycle; source of the older single-study ranges, his advice to log your own cycle and to place diet flexibility late in the luteal phase.

tucker-2025.title: The Effect of the Menstrual Cycle on Energy Intake: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
tucker-2025.support: Fifteen datasets were included consisting of 330 female participants with a mean age of 26 ± 4 years and mean BMI of 22.4 ± 2.3 kg/m2. Overall, there was a statistically significant difference (standardized mean difference = 0.69; P = .039) with increased energy intake in the LP compared with the FP (crude 168 kcal/d average difference between phases). However, there were repeated methodological inconsistencies.

benton-2020.title: Effect of menstrual cycle on resting metabolism: A systematic review and meta-analysis
benton-2020.support: 26 studies involving 318 women were included in the meta-analysis. Overall, there was a small but significant effect favoring increased RMR in the luteal phase (ES = 0.33; 95% CI = 0.17, 0.49). In more recent studies published since 2000, the effect of menstrual phase was reduced and not statistically significant (ES = 0.23; 95% CI = -0.00, 0.47; p = 0.055). Sample sizes were small and studies did not report control of potential confounders.

mcnulty-2020.title: The Effects of Menstrual Cycle Phase on Exercise Performance in Eumenorrheic Women: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
mcnulty-2020.support: Of the 78 included studies, data from 51 studies were eligible for the initial pairwise meta-analysis. The model indicated a trivial effect for both endurance- and strength-based outcomes, with reduced exercise performance observed in the early follicular phase (ES0.5 = -0.06 [95% CrI: -0.16 to 0.04]). The largest effect was identified between the early follicular and the late follicular phases (ES0.5 = -0.14). The quality of evidence was classified as low. General guidelines on exercise performance across the MC cannot be formed; rather, a personalised approach should be taken.

niering-2024.title: The Influence of Menstrual Cycle Phases on Maximal Strength Performance in Healthy Female Adults: A Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis
niering-2024.support: 22 studies met the selection criteria, with a total of 433 subjects. Medium effects (SMD = 0.60; seven studies) for isometric maximal strength in favor of the late follicular phase, small effects (SMD = 0.39; five studies) for isokinetic maximal strength in favor of the ovulation phase, and small effects (SMD = 0.14; three studies) for dynamic maximal strength in favor of the late follicular phase. The results indicate that the early follicular phase is unfavorable for all strength classes.

davidsen-2007.title: Impact of the menstrual cycle on determinants of energy balance: a putative role in weight loss attempts
davidsen-2007.support: In the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle it appears that women's energy intake and energy expenditure are increased and they experience more frequent cravings for foods, particularly those high in carbohydrate and fat, than during the follicular phase. Studies are needed to assess the weight loss outcome of tailoring dietary recommendations and the degree of energy restriction to each menstrual phase.

white-2011.title: Fluid Retention over the Menstrual Cycle: 1-Year Data from the Prospective Ovulation Cohort
white-2011.support: 765 menstrual cycles in 62 healthy women; fluid retention scores peaked on the first day of menstrual flow and were lowest in the mid-follicular period.

blagrove-2020.title: Variations in strength-related measures during the menstrual cycle in eumenorrheic women: A systematic review and meta-analysis
blagrove-2020.journal: Journal of Science and Medicine in Sport
blagrove-2020.support: 21 studies met the criteria for inclusion. Non-significant and small or trivial effect sizes (p≥0.26, Hedges g≤0.35) were identified for all strength-related variables in each comparison between phases. Strength-related measures appear to be minimally altered by the fluctuations in ovarian sex hormones that occur during the menstrual cycle. This finding should be interpreted with caution due to the methodological shortcomings identified by the quality assessment.

colenso-semple-2023.title: Current evidence shows no influence of women's menstrual cycle phase on acute strength performance or adaptations to resistance exercise training
colenso-semple-2023.journal: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
colenso-semple-2023.support: Umbrella review of meta-analyses and systematic reviews. We observed highly variable findings among the published reviews. We noted a pattern of poor and inconsistent methodological practices in the literature. In our opinion, it is premature to conclude that short-term fluctuations in reproductive hormones appreciably influence acute exercise performance or longer-term strength or hypertrophic adaptations to RET.

mcdonald-research-on-women.title: Research on Women - Why Isn't There More?
mcdonald-research-on-women.support: Backs the reasons he gives for the thin research base, the carbohydrate-loading case as a body-size effect, the smaller calorie budget point and the note that diet research mostly enrols women.

geiker-2016.title: A weight-loss program adapted to the menstrual cycle increases weight loss in healthy, overweight, premenopausal women: a 6-mo randomized controlled trial
geiker-2016.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
geiker-2016.support: A total of 60 healthy, overweight, premenopausal women were included in a 6-mo weight-loss program in which each subject consumed a diet of 1600 kcal/d. Thirty-one women (19 Menstralean and 12 control women) completed the study. In an intention-to-treat analysis, the Menstralean group did not achieve a clinically significant weight loss compared with that of the control group (P = 0.61). In per-protocol analyses, a more-pronounced weight loss of 4.3 ± 1.4 kg was shown in adherent Menstralean subjects than in the control group.

elliott-sale-2020.title: The Effects of Oral Contraceptives on Exercise Performance in Women: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
elliott-sale-2020.support: 42 studies and 590 participants were included. Most studies (83%) were graded as moderate, low or very low quality. OCP use might result in slightly inferior exercise performance on average when compared to naturally menstruating women, although any group-level effect is most likely to be trivial. The current evidence does not warrant general guidance on OCP use compared with non-use. Exercise performance was consistent across the OCP cycle.

nolan-2024.title: The Effect of Hormonal Contraceptive Use on Skeletal Muscle Hypertrophy, Power and Strength Adaptations to Resistance Exercise Training: A Systematic Review and Multilevel Meta-analysis
nolan-2024.support: 8 articles (54 effects and 325 participants) met the inclusion criteria. All included studies investigated oral contraceptive pills, with no study including participants using other forms of HC. OCP use does not have a significant effect on hypertrophy (0.01, 95% CI [-0.11, 0.13]), power (-0.04) or strength (0.10, 95% CI [-0.08, 0.28]). There is no evidence-based rationale to advocate for or against the use of OCPs in females partaking in resistance exercise training.

gallo-2014.title: Combination contraceptives: effects on weight
gallo-2014.support: We found 49 trials that met our inclusion criteria. The four trials with a placebo or no intervention group did not find evidence supporting a causal association between combination oral contraceptives or a combination skin patch and weight change. Available evidence was insufficient to determine the effect of combination contraceptives on weight, but no large effect was evident.

lopez-2016.title: Progestin-only contraceptives: effects on weight
lopez-2016.support: We found 22 eligible studies that included a total of 11,450 women. We considered the overall quality of evidence to be low. These 22 studies showed limited evidence of change in weight or body composition with use of POCs. Mean weight gain at 6 or 12 months was less than 2 kg (4.4 lb) for most studies.

authors: Law T Sr, Thuma JR (technical assistance)
loucks-1998.title: Low energy availability, not stress of exercise, alters LH pulsatility in exercising women
loucks-1998.support: Nine young, habitually sedentary, regularly menstruating women after 4 days of intense exercise, with energy availabilities set at 45 and 10 kcal/kg LBM/day. In the exercising women, low energy availability reduced LH pulse frequency by 10%. The stress of exercise neither reduced LH pulse frequency nor increased LH pulse amplitude (all P > 0.4). These results contradict the hypothesis that LH pulsatility is disrupted by exercise stress and suggest that LH pulsatility in women depends on energy availability.

mcdonald-history-women-sport-2.title: A History of Women in Sport: Part 2
mcdonald-history-women-sport-2.support: His account of how late strength sports opened to women, that under-eating and not training explains lost cycles, and that muscular elite athletes reflect selection, not an effect of sport.

teixeira-2018.title: Prevalence of urinary incontinence in female athletes: a systematic review with meta-analysis
teixeira-2018.support: Eight studies met the eligibility criteria. Meta-analysis showed a 36% prevalence of UI in female athletes in different sports, and compared with sedentary women, the athletes had a 177% higher risk of presenting with UI.

wikander-2021.title: Urinary Incontinence in Competitive Women Powerlifters: A Cross-Sectional Survey
wikander-2021.support: Online survey completed by 480 competitive women powerlifters aged between 20 and 71 years. 43.9% of women had experienced UI within the three months prior. The deadlift was the most likely, and the bench-press the least likely exercise to provoke UI. ISI scores were positively correlated with parity, age, competition total and body mass index. There was no significant correlation between ISI and years strength training. Women who had undergone a pelvic floor examination or were confident in correctly performing pelvic floor exercises experienced less severe UI.

cowley-2021.title: “Invisible Sportswomen”: The Sex Data Gap in Sport and Exercise Science Research
cowley-2021.journal: Women in Sport and Physical Activity Journal
cowley-2021.support: About 5,261 publications and 12,511,386 participants were included in the analyses. Sixty-three percentage of publications included both males and females, 31% included males only, and 6% included females only. A total of 8,253,236 (66%) were male and 4,254,445 (34%) were female. Females remain significantly underrepresented within sport and exercise science research.

costello-2014.title: Where are all the female participants in Sports and Exercise Medicine research?
costello-2014.support: Data were extracted from 1382 articles involving a total of 6,076,580 participants. A total of 2,366,968 (39%) participants were female and 3,709,612 (61%) were male. The average percentage of female participants per article across the journals ranged from 35% to 37%.

ose-2025.title: Where Are All the Female Participants in Sports and Exercise Medicine Research? A Decade Later
ose-2025.journal: The American Journal of Sports Medicine
ose-2025.support: A total of 1441 studies and 40,152,860 participants were included, 17,648,509 (43.95%) female. 103 (7.15%) studies included only female participants compared with 268 (18.6%) male-only studies. A total of 66 (5.6%) studies included menstrual-status considerations in their study design.

tarnopolsky-1995.title: Carbohydrate loading and metabolism during exercise in men and women
tarnopolsky-1995.support: Similarly trained male (n = 7) and female (n = 8) endurance athletes; dietary carbohydrate raised from 55-60 to 75% of energy intake for 4 days. The men increased muscle glycogen concentration by 41% and had a corresponding increase in performance time (45%), whereas the women did not increase glycogen concentration (0%) or performance time (5%).

tarnopolsky-2001.title: Gender differences in carbohydrate loading are related to energy intake
tarnopolsky-2001.support: Well-trained men (n = 6) and women (n = 6) on three diets: habitual; high carbohydrate (75%); and extra energy + CHO (about 34% more). Total glycogen concentration was higher for the men on the CHO and CHO + E trials compared with Hab, whereas women increased only on the CHO + E trial. There were no gender differences in hexokinase activity. A low energy intake may explain the previously reported lower capacity for women to glycogen load compared with men.

pagoto-2012.title: Male Inclusion in Randomized Controlled Trials of Lifestyle Weight Loss Interventions
pagoto-2012.support: Randomized controlled trials of lifestyle weight loss interventions (N = 244 studies with a total of 95,207 participants) published 1999-2009. Samples were on average 27% male vs. 73% female. About 32% of trials used exclusively female samples, whereas only 5% used exclusively male samples.

mcdonald-history-women-sport.title: A History of Women in Sport
mcdonald-history-women-sport.support: His account that early medical objections to women's sport were assertions never tested, and that examinations of sportswomen at the time found no harm.

gardner-2007.title: Comparison of the Atkins, Zone, Ornish, and LEARN Diets for Change in Weight and Related Risk Factors Among Overweight Premenopausal Women
gardner-2007.support: Twelve-month randomized trial among 311 free-living, overweight/obese (body mass index, 27-40) nondiabetic, premenopausal women assigned to Atkins (n = 77), Zone (n = 79), LEARN (n = 79), or Ornish (n = 76) diets, with weekly instruction for 2 months, then 10-month follow-up. Mean 12-month weight loss: Atkins, -4.7 kg (95% CI, -6.3 to -3.1 kg), Zone, -1.6 kg (-2.8 to -0.4 kg), LEARN, -2.6 kg (-3.8 to -1.3 kg), and Ornish, -2.2 kg (-3.6 to -0.8 kg). Weight loss was not statistically different among the Zone, LEARN, and Ornish groups. Erratum (JAMA 298:178) checked: corrected LEARN and Ornish values match these.

mcdonald-comparison-of-diets.title: Comparison of the Atkins, Zone, Ornish and LEARN Diets
mcdonald-comparison-of-diets.support: His critique of reading the A TO Z trial as a metabolic advantage: self-reported intake, early water loss, the stall after the class period, small absolute losses, and low-carb as a fit for insulin resistance.

hall-2017.title: Obesity Energetics: Body Weight Regulation and the Effects of Diet Composition
hall-2017.support: While low-carbohydrate diets have been suggested to partially subvert these processes by increasing energy expenditure and promoting fat loss, our meta-analysis of 32 controlled feeding studies with isocaloric substitution of carbohydrate for fat found that both energy expenditure (26 kcal/d; P <.0001) and fat loss (16 g/d; P <.0001) were greater with lower fat diets.

gardner-2018.title: Effect of Low-Fat vs Low-Carbohydrate Diet on 12-Month Weight Loss in Overweight Adults and the Association With Genotype Pattern or Insulin Secretion
gardner-2018.support: 609 adults; weight change at 12 months was -5.3 kg for low-fat vs -6.0 kg for low-carbohydrate (difference 0.7 kg, 95% CI -0.2 to 1.6).

alhassan-2008.title: Dietary adherence and weight loss success among overweight women: results from the A TO Z weight loss study
alhassan-2008.support: Secondary analysis using data from 181 free-living overweight/obese women in the A TO Z study (Atkins, Zone and Ornish). Within each diet group, adherence score was significantly correlated with 12-month weight change (r = 0.42, 0.34 and 0.38). Twelve-month weight change in the most vs least adherent tertiles was -8.3 vs -1.9 kg (Atkins); -3.7 vs -0.4 kg (Zone) and -6.5 vs -1.7 kg (Ornish). Strategies to increase adherence may deserve more emphasis than the specific macronutrient composition of the weight loss diet itself.

mcclain-2013.title: Adherence to a low-fat vs. low-carbohydrate diet differs by insulin resistance status
mcclain-2013.support: Secondary analyses among 81 free-living, overweight/obese women. IR participants were less likely to adhere and lose weight on a LF-diet compared to insulin-sensitive participants assigned to the same diet. There were no significant differences between IR and IS participants assigned to LC-diet in relative adherence or weight loss.

mcdonald-fat-loss-supplements.title: Do Fat Loss Supplements Work?
mcdonald-fat-loss-supplements.support: His view that few fat-loss compounds work, that effects are small and none is required, his warnings on stimulant misuse and yohimbine, and the note on slower caffeine clearance in women on the pill.

zsiboras-2018.title: Capsaicin and capsiate could be appropriate agents for treatment of obesity: A meta-analysis of human studies
zsiboras-2018.journal: Critical Reviews in Food Science and Nutrition
zsiboras-2018.support: Of the 627 trials identified, 9 provided results suitable to be included in analysis. After ingestion of capsaicin or capsinoids the energy expenditure increased (245 kJ/day, 58.56 kcal/day, p = 0.030). Studies with mean BMI of the participants below 25 kg/m2 failed to report any effect on the energy expenditure.

jurgens-2012.title: Green tea for weight loss and weight maintenance in overweight or obese adults
jurgens-2012.support: Green tea preparations appear to induce a small, statistically non-significant weight loss in overweight or obese adults. Because the amount of weight loss is small, it is not likely to be clinically important. Green tea had no significant effect on the maintenance of weight loss.

tabrizi-2019.title: The effects of caffeine intake on weight loss: a systematic review and dos-response meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
tabrizi-2019.journal: Critical Reviews in Food Science and Nutrition
tabrizi-2019.support: Thirteen RCTs with 606 participants were included in the meta-analyses. For every doubling in caffeine intake, the mean reduction in weight, BMI, and fat mass increased, corresponding to 22, 17, and 28 percent, respectively (I2 above 90%). Caffeine intake might promote weight, BMI and body fat reduction.

mielgo-ayuso-2014.title: Effects of dietary supplementation with epigallocatechin-3-gallate on weight loss, energy homeostasis, cardiometabolic risk factors and liver function in obese women: randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial
mielgo-ayuso-2014.support: Eighty-three obese pre-menopausal women consumed 300 mg/d of EGCG or placebo. We did not find any significant difference in the changes in body weight (-0.3 kg, 95% CI -5.0, 4.3), fat mass (-0.7 kg, 95% CI -3.5, 2.1). Dietary supplementation with 300 mg/d of EGCG for 12 weeks did not enhance energy-restricted diet-induced adiposity reductions.

dostal-2016.title: Long-Term Supplementation of Green Tea Extract Does Not Modify Adiposity or Bone Mineral Density in a Randomized Trial of Overweight and Obese Postmenopausal Women
dostal-2016.support: 12-mo randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 937 postmenopausal women assigned to GTE containing 843 mg EGCG or placebo; this substudy was conducted in 121 overweight/obese participants. There were no differences in changes in BMI, total fat mass (-0.30 compared with -0.12 kg; P = 0.40), percentage of body fat (P = 0.99), or BMD over 12 mo.

yu-2017.title: Effect of Green Tea Supplements on Liver Enzyme Elevation: Results from a Randomized Intervention Study in the United States
yu-2017.support: 1,021 participants (513 in GTE and 508 in placebo arm) with normal baseline levels of liver enzymes. Overall, 26 (5.1%) women in GTE developed moderate or more severe abnormalities in any liver function measure during the intervention period, yielding an OR of 7.0 (95% CI, 2.4-20.3). ALT returned to normal after dechallenge and increased again after one or more rechallenges with GTE.

abernethy-1985.title: Impairment of caffeine clearance by chronic use of low-dose oestrogen-containing oral contraceptives
abernethy-1985.support: Treated females matched with 9 non-smoking, drug-free, healthy control females. Each subject received 162 mg caffeine base orally. OCS subjects had a prolonged elimination half-life of caffeine (mean 7.88 h vs 5.37 h in the controls), the result of marked impairment of the plasma clearance of caffeine. With chronic caffeine consumption, OCS users are predicted to have an increased steady-state plasma caffeine concentration.

lane-1992.title: Menstrual cycle effects on caffeine elimination in the human female
lane-1992.support: Repeated 24-hour caffeine elimination studies during the follicular and luteal phases in 10 healthy women. Systemic clearance of caffeine was slower in the luteal phase, although the t1/2 did not differ. The effect may be too small to be of clinical significance in the majority of women.

purdue-smithe-2016.title: A prospective study of caffeine and coffee intake and premenstrual syndrome
purdue-smithe-2016.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
purdue-smithe-2016.support: Case-control study nested within the prospective Nurses' Health Study II; PMS cases (n = 1234), controls (n = 2426). After adjustment, total caffeine intake was not associated with PMS. The OR comparing women with the highest (quintile median = 543 mg/d) to the lowest (quintile median = 18 mg/d) caffeine intake was 0.79 (95% CI: 0.61, 1.04).

shekelle-2003.title: Efficacy and Safety of Ephedra and Ephedrine for Weight Loss and Athletic Performance
shekelle-2003.support: No weight loss trials assessed duration of treatment greater than 6 months. Pooled results for placebo comparisons with ephedrine (n = 5), ephedrine and caffeine (n = 12) yielded estimates of weight loss (more than placebo) of 0.6 and 1.0 kg/mo. Safety data from 50 trials yielded estimates of 2.2- to 3.6-fold increases in odds of psychiatric, autonomic, or gastrointestinal symptoms, and heart palpitations. Ephedrine and ephedra promote modest short-term weight loss (approximately 0.9 kg/mo more than placebo).

kucio-1991.title: Does yohimbine act as a slimming drug?
kucio-1991.support: Twenty female obese outpatients on a low-energy diet (1,000 kcal/day): 10 received 5 mg yohimbine per os 4 times a day and 10 a placebo for 3 weeks. Mean weight loss 3.55 kg (yohimbine) vs. 2.21 kg (placebo), P less than 0.005. No significant effect of yohimbine on lipolysis was observed.

mcdonald-melatonin.title: 3 Less Well Known Benefits of Melatonin for Women
mcdonald-melatonin.support: His survey of melatonin trials in postmenopausal women and in polycystic ovary syndrome, his criticism of percentage-only reporting, and his statement that use for premenstrual symptoms is untested.

amstrup-2016.title: Reduced fat mass and increased lean mass in response to 1 year of melatonin treatment in postmenopausal women: A randomized placebo-controlled trial
amstrup-2016.support: We randomized 81 postmenopausal women to 1 year of treatment with melatonin (1 or 3 mg nightly) or placebo. Fat mass decreased in the melatonin group by 6.9% (95% CI: 1.4%; 12.4%, P = 0.02) compared to placebo. A borderline significant increase in lean mass of 5.2% was found (P = 0.08). After adjusting for BMI, lean mass increased by 2.6% (P = 0.04). Changes in body weight and BMI did not differ between groups.

amstrup-2015.title: Melatonin improves bone mineral density at the femoral neck in postmenopausal women with osteopenia: a randomized controlled trial
amstrup-2015.support: We randomized 81 postmenopausal osteopenic women to 1-yr nightly treatment with melatonin 1 mg (N = 20), 3 mg (N = 20), or placebo (N = 41). Compared to placebo, femoral neck BMD increased by 1.4% in response to melatonin (P < 0.05) in a dose-dependent manner, as BMD increased by 0.5% in the 1 mg/day group (P = 0.55) and by 2.3% (P < 0.01) in the 3 mg/day group. Treatment did not significantly affect BMD at other sites.

maria-2017.title: Melatonin-micronutrients Osteopenia Treatment Study (MOTS): a translational study assessing melatonin, strontium (citrate), vitamin D3 and vitamin K2 (MK7) on bone density, bone marker turnover and health related quality of life in postmenopausal osteopenic women following a one-year double-blind RCT and on osteoblast-osteoclast co-cultures
maria-2017.support: One-year double blind randomized control trial of nightly melatonin, strontium (citrate), vitamin D3 and vitamin K2 (MSDK) in postmenopausal osteopenic women (ages 49-75). Compared to placebo, MSDK treatment increased BMD in lumbar spine (4.3%) and left femoral neck (2.2%). Mood and sleep quality improved for the MSDK group.

treister-goltzman-2021.title: Melatonin and the health of menopausal women: A systematic review
treister-goltzman-2021.support: Twenty-four studies were included, with 1,173 participants. There is some evidence that very low-density lipoprotein and triglycerides levels increase during melatonin administration. There is a fair amount of evidence that melatonin treatment has a favorable effect on bone density and BMI. Melatonin treatment improves EEG patterns and subjective sleep quality in postmenopausal women with preexisting sleep impairment. In a dose of 3 mg and above, melatonin improves climacteric symptoms in one or more domains.

ziaei-2024.title: Effect of melatonin supplementation on cardiometabolic risk factors, oxidative stress and hormonal profile in PCOS patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials
ziaei-2024.support: Six studies met the inclusion criteria. Melatonin intake significantly increased TAC levels and has no effect on FBS, insulin, HOMA-IR, TC, TG, HDL, LDL, MDA, hs-CRP, mFG, SHBG, total testosterone, and pregnancy rate in patients with PCOS compared to controls. The clear effect of melatonin supplementation needs to be evaluated further in large populations and long-term RCTs.

jamilian-2019.title: Effects of Melatonin Supplementation on Hormonal, Inflammatory, Genetic, and Oxidative Stress Parameters in Women With Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
jamilian-2019.support: Randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial among 56 patients with PCOS, aged 18-40: 5 mg melatonin supplements (n = 28) or placebo (n = 28) twice a day for 12 weeks. Melatonin administration significantly reduced hirsutism, serum total testosterone and hs-CRP compared with the placebo.

pengelly-2025.title: Iron deficiency, supplementation, and sports performance in female athletes: A systematic review
pengelly-2025.journal: Journal of Sport and Health Science
pengelly-2025.support: Up to 60% of female athletes experience iron deficiency. A total of 23 studies comprising 669 athletes across 16 sports were included; iron deficient defined as serum ferritin < 40 µg/L. Iron deficiency negatively affects endurance performance by 3%-4%. Isokinetic strength and anaerobic power performance may be impeded among ID athletes, but the effect of FeSup on anaerobic power varied markedly. Most studies (n = 18) contained group sizes of 20 athletes or fewer.
